Adding technical detail from initial triage:

On Thu Jun 7 2028 17:04–17:40 PT we observed a cluster-wide p99 increase on streaming nodes serving the us-west region for the model family mentioned by Ava. Early indicators:
- burst of small concurrent connections (~+2.8x) that increased KV cache churn and reduced effective batching efficiency
- downstream slowdowns from a host-level kernel fallback on a subset (approx 12%) of the GPU pool due to a quantized-kernel compatibility regression introduced in a build last week
- autoscaler shows healthy scale-ups, but scaling lag and queue head-of-line blocking led to elevated tail latency for long-lived SSE connections

Immediate mitigations performed (16:50 PT):
- Rolled back the runtime kernel change for the affected variant to restore previous execution path (rollback ID: rb_20280607_kern01) — this reduced single-request p99 in canary by ~60% in the first 10 minutes.
- Applied an emergency routing rule to move Lark traffic to a sibling model shard with reserved capacity (route: shard-usw-4 -> reserved-Lark) to guarantee throughput for their tenant.
- Enabled a temporary aggressive KV cache retention policy for the swarm to reduce cache misses under churn.

Current status (16:42 PT): partial restoration — p99 improved but still above SLO during highest concurrency window. We're watching the queueing metrics and will continue to scale and drain queues.

Requested from Lark: examples of failing session IDs and any client-side reconnect patterns.

I'll post a follow-up with logs attached.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Thank you all — and Tim, apologies for the disruption. Quick executive summary and asks: 

Summary (what we know):
- Root cause (probable): recent runtime kernel change degraded quantized execution path for a portion of the GPU fleet under high-churn SSE workloads, increasing per-connection CPU/GPU scheduling time and KV cache misses.
- Immediate mitigations: Dev rolled back the kernel, moved Lark to reserved shard, and adjusted KV cache retention. Partial improvement observed; full stability requires draining queues and an additional safe patch.

Proposed next steps and ETA:
1) Our SREs will perform a full patch (tested) and a controlled canary today night — ETA for full remediation: 8–12 hours.
2) We'll run a targeted autoscaler policy update and increase reserved capacity for Lark for the next 72 hours to avoid repeat impact during their peak windows.
3) Post-incident RCA will include the kernel regression details, test gap, and a proposed change to preflight model-variant compatibility checks. Draft RCA due in 3 business days.

On credits/exec action: I authorize Customer Success to offer a one-time service credit for the impacted window; Marissa, please propose a concrete range and we will finalize via Legal. If Lark requests a short-term dedicated capacity (Dedicated/Reserved) we should prioritize the sales motion — speak to Product to scope.

Tim — we will keep you updated every hour until full remediation. Thank you for the partnership and for surfacing trace samples; Dev, please post the matching trace ids and final log bundle when available.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
VP Engineering, Redwood Inference
